project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 277 (System persists the revision cap used per cycle, raising M to 40 once the pool holds 50 or more worlds)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 277 in the existing dreaming member (packages/dreaming, import name dreaming; seat src/app/modules/dreaming): the top rung of docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §12.1's pool-size ladder and the per-cycle persistence of it. Two halves in one new module, dreaming/cap.py. (1) The schedule — revision_cap(world_count, *, floor=20, full_dreaming=50), a pure judgment over a count the caller already has (the same verdict-gate shape feature 275's rejects_thin_pool takes): 10 (CAPPED_SWEEP_CAP) on the 20–50 rung, 40 (FULL_DREAMING_CAP) once the pool holds 50 or more worlds (FULL_DREAMING_WORLDS), and a refusal below the floor delegated to feature 275's own rejects_thin_pool so the bottom rung is refused in the floor's own word (pool_too_thin) by the floor's own one spelling — which is what depends_on 275 means in code. 40 is the figure §12.1 itself computes the bar with ("At M = 40 (bar ≈ 2.72) … n > 53 worlds"), and 50 is the M3 precondition's own threshold ("≥ 50 worlds in the pool (§12.1)"); the middle rung's 10 is §12.1's "capped at 8–10" at the count feature 276's refusal fixes, stated here as the band's cap so the ladder has one spelling — feature 276 is a sibling (both depend on 275 only) and is not imported, cannot be imported, and does not exist yet at the time this lands. (2) The record — record_cycle_cap(iteration_id, world_count, *, floor=…, full_dreaming=…, database_url=None, recorded_at=None, env=None) writes one row per cycle into this member's own lazily-created cycle_cap table (CYCLE_CAP_TABLE, member-owned like pool_freeze, never in the shared migration chain): the row carries the iteration, the instant (the member's one stamp shape, UTC truncated to the second), the pool size the cap was decided over, and the cap — which the record DECIDES (the caller cannot hand one in), so a row can never disagree with the ladder. cycle_caps(*, database_url=None, env=None) is the audit read: every record, oldest first, ordered by (recorded_at, id). The cap is persisted rather than remembered because Appendix B's selection bar (advantage > √(2 ln M) · σ_V / √n_worlds — feature 280's test) reads M back, and a bar computed over an M nobody recorded is a bar over a number nobody ran. The table is append-only with no unique index and no triggers (a cap is a judgment, not a hold) and its ids are minted per occurrence (sha256 over iteration, instant and a draw) so a retried cycle recorded inside the same second never collides on the primary key — the lesson cycle.py's _hold_id states for holds. Two new error siblings under DreamingError: CapRequestError (the ask's own facts — malformed id, figure, rung, instant, or URL) and CapRecordError (the store's facts — a database that holds no pool to cap, refused BEFORE the table is created so a refusal leaves no trace; or a row whose stamp will not read back). The member's one spellings of the shared rules (validated_iteration_id, sqlite_path, _stamp, _parsed_instant — all in dreaming.cycle) are reused and their refusals are translated at the cap's seam, so a caller of the cap never meets feature 270's FreezeRequestError or PoolFrozenError for an act that held nothing. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited; no new @register component is added (feature 270's single "dreaming" component is untouched); the member joins by workspace-scan convention and does not import another workspace member.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in src/app/modules/ <member>/ are reached by namespace import (e.g. app.modules.dreaming). A member never imports another member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly (run both `uv run pytest tests/` and the member's own `packages/dreaming/tests/`). Measure the real numbers by running the suite before relying on them. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling. The dreaming member is stdlib-only, and feature 277 keeps it that way: hashlib, secrets, sqlite3, datetime, os.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, hand-written __slots__ value classes for store records (the member's FreezeRecord precedent), docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/alpha-engine-prd.md / docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, stdlib-only computation, `@register` only in the package `__init__` (never a submodule — a submodule's registration fires only on the first `create_app()` of a process), degrade-don't-break composition, member-owned tables created lazily beside the only module that writes them (never in the shared migration chain, which is order-sensitive and excluded from this feature's file claim), per-occurrence row ids so a retried window never collides on the primary key, the §12 ordering rule (ordered history reads), and the error-vocabulary discipline that no member imports another and a caller must be able to catch one feature's refusal without catching a neighbouring feature's (translate at the seam). Features 270 (the cycle freeze, cycle.py), 275 (the ladder floor, ladder.py) already live in this member; feature 277 is a third sentence within it, not a new member. Feature 276 (the 20–50 ceiling refusal) is a parallel sibling and MUST NOT be imported or assumed present.

category.name: Dreaming Loop & Meta-Selection
category.feature: System persists the revision cap used per cycle, raising M to 40 once the pool holds 50 or more worlds.

project_specification.integration_points: The schedule and the record are free functions in the dreaming member's new cap module, reached directly from the member (`from dreaming import revision_cap, record_cycle_cap, cycle_caps, CapRecord, CapRequestError, CapRecordError, FULL_DREAMING_WORLDS, FULL_DREAMING_CAP, CAPPED_SWEEP_CAP, CYCLE_CAP_TABLE, cycle_cap_schema`) and re-exported by the member __init__, the way feature 275's floor names are. No composed application needs a second component: feature 270's single "dreaming" component (the CycleFreeze) is untouched, and the seat (src/app/modules/dreaming) is not edited — the floor set that precedent and feature 277 follows it. The count the schedule reads is the pool's size, which the member already computes (pool_commitment returns (digest, world_count) and a feature-270 hold records world_count at the moment it opened); in the loop the caller holds the figure from freeze.open()'s FreezeRecord and hands it to record_cycle_cap, so the count is never performed twice and the record never counts the pool — it only refuses (via layout.pool_tables_present, a sqlite_master probe that reads no pool row) a database that holds no pool at all. Feature 280's bar and the M-revision sweep (features 271-274) read M back from the record via cycle_caps(); the table lives in the same database the replay pool and pool_freeze live in (DATABASE_URL, sqlite:///), resolved the way open_cycle_freeze resolves it: an explicit URL first, then the deployment environment, then a named refusal when neither names one.
project_specification.constraints: - The revision cap is decided by the schedule, never accepted from the caller: the row's revision_cap is always revision_cap()'s answer over the row's world_count, so a record can never disagree with §12.1's ladder. - The boundary is exact and inclusive: world_count >= 50 answers 40 (FULL_DREAMING_CAP); 20 <= world_count < 50 answers 10 (CAPPED_SWEEP_CAP); world_count < 20 is refused by feature 275's own rejects_thin_pool in its own word (pool_too_thin) — the floor keyword passes straight through to the ladder's gate so the two spellings of the bottom rung cannot disagree. - Feature 276 is a parallel sibling: this feature MUST NOT import it, reference its module, or assume it has landed. The shared 10 is the PRD's figure, spelled here as the band's cap constant. - The schedule is a judgment over a count, not a count the feature performs: revision_cap takes the figure and opens no database; the record takes the figure too and reads no pool row — it only probes table presence, and refuses (before creating anything) a database that holds no pool. - Two new error siblings under DreamingError — CapRequestError (the ask) and CapRecordError (the store) — that borrow none of the member's existing three classes and are borrowed by none of them. The member's one spellings of the shared rules (iteration id, sqlite URL, stamp format, all in dreaming.cycle) are reused with their refusals translated at the cap's seam. Neither new class carries a code word; the one thin-pool refusal the record mints is feature 275's, delegated, in feature 275's word. - One row per cycle-occurrence: append-only, per-occurrence ids (a retry in the same second is a second row, never an overwrite or a primary-key collision), no unique index, no triggers, history ordered by (recorded_at, id). The table is member-owned, created lazily beside the only module that writes it, never in the shared migration chain. - No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited. No new @register component and no seat export: feature 270's single "dreaming" component is the member's whole composition and its suite (test_component.py) is untouched. - All existing tests in the dreaming member (packages/dreaming/tests) and in tests/ must stay green. The member's own suite must be run explicitly (it is not graded by the bare `uv run pytest` gate). - Do not edit the order-sensitive shared files: src/app/middleware.py, src/app/settings.py, migrations/versions/**, alembic/versions/**.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1 — the vocabulary and the schedule. Add CapRequestError and CapRecordError to dreaming.errors as siblings of the member's existing three under DreamingError. Add dreaming/cap.py with the constants (FULL_DREAMING_WORLDS = 50, FULL_DREAMING_CAP = 40, CAPPED_SWEEP_CAP = 10, CYCLE_CAP_TABLE = "cycle_cap"), cycle_cap_schema() returning the idempotent one-table DDL as text (no triggers, no unique index, the persistence rationale in the schema comment), and revision_cap() — a pure function validating the figure (CapRequestError for a malformed one, bool refused), the floor (delegated to ladder.validated_floor, in the ladder's vocabulary), and the boundary (CapRequestError, including a boundary below the floor, which would erase the middle rung), then delegating the thin judgment to rejects_thin_pool and answering 40 at or above the boundary and 10 below it.

Phase 2 — the record and the read. In dreaming/cap.py add CapRecord (hand-written __slots__, the row's five facts, the member's stamp shape parsed back with the refusal translated to CapRecordError), record_cycle_cap() — validate the ask, decide the cap by the schedule, resolve the store (explicit URL, then DATABASE_URL, then a named CapRequestError), probe pool presence before any DDL so a refusal leaves no trace (CapRecordError), insert one row with a per-occurrence id, and return the record — and cycle_caps() — the ordered history read over the same resolution and probe. Re-export everything from the member __init__ and extend the member docstring with the third sentence. Reuse validated_iteration_id, sqlite_path, _stamp and _parsed_instant from dreaming.cycle with their refusals translated at the seam.

Phase 3 — the tests and verification. Add packages/dreaming/tests/ test_cap.py pinning: the exact boundary (49 → 10, 50 → 40), the three rungs, the constants against §12.1's figures, the delegated thin refusal (pool_too_thin, §12.1 named), the pure-function shape, the floor/boundary parameters and their validation (a boundary below the floor refused), the record's decide-then-persist contract (row cap always equals revision_cap(figure)), persistence and read-back equality, ordered history, the retry-is-a-new-occurrence law, the lazy table creation, the empty history over an untouched pool, every refusal (thin, malformed id, naive instant, no URL, unspeakable URL, no pool — each in the right class, each leaving nothing written), the schema text (five columns, IF NOT EXISTS, no TRIGGER, no UNIQUE), and the vocabulary siblinghood. Extend test_errors.py with the cap pair's sibling test. Run the member suite (uv run pytest packages/dreaming/tests) and the repository-level suite (uv run pytest tests/) — both — and lint only the changed files against a sibling.
